biography: Felipe Kiemann's story is steeped in the dust and roar of Brazilian stock car racing. Growing up in the shadow of Interlagos, he spent his childhood glued to the fence, dreaming of emulating Senna. His father, a mechanic for a local Copa Fusca team, provided the spark, teaching Felipe the intricacies of the air-cooled engine. He began his racing career at 16, competing in karting events across Sao Paulo state. A defining moment came during the 2012 Copa Fusca season finale at Curitiba when, starting from the back of the grid due to a qualifying mishap, he clawed his way to a stunning victory, showcasing his tenacity and car control in the wet. Now, at 34, Kiemann is considered a veteran of the Copa Fusca circuit, known for his calculating precision and uncanny ability to extract every ounce of performance from his aging Volkswagen.
drivingStyle: Kiemann is a master of controlled aggression. He doesn't throw the car into corners; instead, he meticulously analyzes the entry, apex, and exit, maximizing grip and minimizing wheel spin. His tire management is exceptional, often preserving his rubber while rivals fade in the closing laps. He thrives under pressure, exhibiting a remarkable coolness that allows him to make calculated decisions in the heat of battle. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and expertly timed overtakes.

rivalries.reason: Silva, a young up-and-comer, frequently clashes with Kiemann due to their contrasting driving styles - Silva being aggressive and Kiemann being calculating. Their on-track battles are always intense.
Flores and Kiemann have a long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial incident in the 2018 season where Kiemann was accused of intentionally blocking her during qualifying.
Costa, known for his aggressive defense, often finds himself battling Kiemann for track position. Their rivalry is fueled by numerous close calls and accusations of unsportsmanlike conduct.

quirks: Always polishes his helmet visor with a microfiber cloth exactly 15 minutes before each race.
Listens to the same Sepultura album ('Roots') before every race.
Insists on wearing the same lucky socks, even though they're visibly worn and faded.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about brute force; it's about understanding the rhythm of the machine and dancing with it."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2015 Copa Fusca Championship after a season-long battle with his arch-rival, Ricardo Silva. He secured the title by a mere two points after a nail-biting final race at Interlagos.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 2017 season opener at Taruma after a mechanical failure, effectively ending his championship hopes early in the season.
